pattern: Ripple XOR chain in 512-bit parity reduction
strategy: Balanced tree reduction instead of serial cascade
rationale: Serial XOR depth scales linearly (512 stages); a balanced tree reduces it to log₂(512)=9 levels. The measured segment (stages 0–8, 5.2 ns) represents the beginning of a chain where 4 gates at depth 4 take 1.3 ns each—each stage depends on all prior stages. A tree decouples this: all bits pair in parallel at level 0 (depth 1), then pairs of pairs (depth 2), etc. The final output remains identical—XOR of all inputs—but arrives 50× deeper in the logic instead of 500×, so the first few stages now run at ~0.5–0.6 ns each rather than ~1.3 ns.
target: Lines 322–329 (par_chain ripple generate loop and par_chain_out assignment)
area_cost: small: a balanced tree uses the same total number of XOR gates (511 gates for 512 inputs, one fewer than the ripple chain, actually), just reorganized in width instead of depth.
equivalence_argument: The ripple chain computes par_chain[XW] = xd_q[0] ⊕ xd_q[1] ⊕ … ⊕ xd_q[XW-1]. The balanced tree pairs all inputs, then recursively XORs the results, computing the same final XOR. Reset is identical: xfrm_par_par_chain_out enters a flop clocked on clk_xfrm_div2 with standard asynchronous reset, unchanged. Intermediate widths are all single-bit signals; the tree output is a single bit matching par_chain[XW]. No sign extension or truncation.
